title: Memory and thinking check
intro: Ask the person each question in the language they are most comfortable with. Do not give hints. Mark what they actually said or did.

source.citation: Prince M, et al. A brief dementia screener suitable for use by non-specialists in resource poor settings: the cross-cultural derivation and validation of the brief Community Screening Instrument for Dementia. Int J Geriatr Psychiatry 2011;26(9):899-907.

licence: Items are from the open-access article above (Creative Commons Attribution 2.5; re-use permitted, commercial exploitation not permitted). The parent CSI-D was developed by K. S. Hall and colleagues. Confirm permission and obtain a validated local-language version before any real field use.
wording_status: English administration wording follows the published appendix. No translation is shipped: unvalidated translations of cognitive test items are not acceptable for screening.

items.prompt: First, say: "I am going to tell you three words. Please repeat them and try to remember them: Boat, House, Fish."
items.guide: Repeat the three words until the person can say all three (up to six tries). This step is not scored. You will ask for the words again at the end.

items.prompt: Point to your own elbow and ask: "What do we call this?"
"What do you do with a hammer?"
items.guide: Correct if the answer shows they know its use, for example driving a nail into something.

items.prompt: "Where is the local market or the nearest shop?"
items.guide: Correct if the answer is right for where the person lives.

items.prompt: "What day of the week is it today?"

items.guide: Accept the season name people use locally.

items.prompt: "Please point first to the window and then to the door."
items.guide: Correct only if both are pointed to, in that order.

items.prompt: "Do you remember the three words I told you a few minutes ago?"
items.guide: The words were Boat, House, Fish. Count how many the person recalls without help.
